1 │ # Saved version answers get thrown away when rules are tidied
   2 │ 
   3 │ ## What happens now
   4 │ 
   5 │ When I give a group of version rules and then ask for it as text, the tool tidies the rules by removing repeats and putting them in order. While tidying, it also clears two answers it had already worked out: the answer to "can any version ever match this group" and the answer to "which version ranges does this group cover". The next time I ask whether a version matches, the tool has to work both answers out again from scratch. So a simple request for the text of my rules quietly undoes work the tool had already done.
   6 │ 
   7 │ ## What should happen
   8 │ 
   9 │ After the tool tidies my group of version rules, the answers it already worked out should stay in place. Asking for the text of the group should not clear them. When I then check a version, or repeatedly check versions against the same group, the tool should reuse the answers it already has instead of working them out again.
  10 │ 
  11 │ ## About this project
  12 │ 
  13 │ This project is a Python library that helps people work with version numbers and version requirements, such as the ones written in a package file. It can compare versions, read the rules that describe which versions are allowed, and tell you whether a given version fits those rules. Many other tools depend on it, so it needs to give fast and consistent answers.
  14 │ 
  15 │ ## Problem this solves
  16 │ 
  17 │ When the tool throws away answers it already worked out, every later version check on the same group of rules costs extra time and effort for no reason. People who check many versions against the same rules pay that cost again and again, and they get no benefit from it.

 760 │     format so the same pickle can be loaded in future packaging
 761 │     releases.

 763 │     .. versionchanged:: 26.2
 764 │ 
 765 │         Added a stable pickle format. Pickles created with
 766 │         packaging 26.2+ can be unpickled with future releases.
 767 │         Backward compatibility with pickles from
 768 │         packaging < 26.2 is supported but may be removed in a future
 769 │         release.

 773 │         "_canonicalized",
 774 │         "_has_arbitrary",

 781 │     def __init__(
 782 │         self,
 783 │         specifiers: str | Iterable[Specifier] = "",
 784 │         prereleases: bool | None = None,
 785 │     ) -> None:
 786 │         """Initialize a SpecifierSet instance.
 787 │ 
 788 │         :param specifiers:
 789 │             The string representation of a specifier or a comma-separated list of
 790 │             specifiers which will be parsed and normalized before use.
 791 │             May also be an iterable of ``Specifier`` instances, which will be used
 792 │             as is.
 793 │         :param prereleases:
 794 │             This tells the SpecifierSet if it should accept prerelease versions if
 795 │             applicable or not. The default of ``None`` will autodetect it from the
 796 │             given specifiers.
 797 │ 
 798 │         :raises InvalidSpecifier:
 799 │             If the given ``specifiers`` are not parseable than this exception will be
 800 │             raised.
 801 │         """
 802 │ 
 803 │         if isinstance(specifiers, str):
 804 │             # Split on `,` to break each individual specifier into its own item, and
 805 │             # strip each item to remove leading/trailing whitespace.
 806 │             split_specifiers = [s.strip() for s in specifiers.split(",") if s.strip()]
 807 │ 
 808 │             self._specs: tuple[Specifier, ...] = tuple(map(Specifier, split_specifiers))
 809 │             # Fast substring check; avoids iterating parsed specs.
 810 │             self._has_arbitrary = "===" in specifiers
 811 │         else:
 812 │             self._specs = tuple(specifiers)
 813 │             # Substring check works for both Specifier objects and plain
 814 │             # strings (setuptools passes lists of strings).
 815 │             self._has_arbitrary = any("===" in str(s) for s in self._specs)
 816 │ 
 817 │         self._canonicalized = len(self._specs) <= 1
 818 │         self._is_unsatisfiable: bool | None = None
 819 │         self._ranges: Sequence[VersionRange] | None = None
 820 │ 
 821 │         # Store our prereleases value so we can use it later to determine if
 822 │         # we accept prereleases or not.
 823 │         self._prereleases = prereleases

 826 │         """Deduplicate, sort, and cache specs for order-sensitive operations."""
 827 │         if not self._canonicalized:
 828 │             self._specs = tuple(dict.fromkeys(sorted(self._specs, key=str)))
 829 │             self._canonicalized = True
 830 │             self._is_unsatisfiable = None

Done.

## What the ticket asked
`SpecifierSet` tidies its spec rules (dedupe + sort) inside `_canonical_specs()` whenever `str()`/`__hash__`/`__eq__` run. That method also wiped the two lazily-computed answers — `_is_unsatisfiable` ("can any version ever match") and `_ranges` ("which version ranges does this cover") — so later `contains()` calls had to recompute them.

## Fix
`src/packaging/specifiers.py` — `SpecifierSet._canonical_specs()` no longer resets `_is_unsatisfiable` / `_ranges`. Reordering and deduping specs leaves the intersected ranges and the unsatisfiability verdict unchanged, so the caches are safely kept. Behavior/text output is unchanged.

## Verification
- Targeted: `python -m pytest tests/test_specifiers.py -k "canonicalization_keeps" -q` — both seeded tests now pass (previously 2 failed).
- Full file: `python -m pytest tests/test_specifiers.py -q` → `1691 passed in 4.01s`.
- Full suite (background, log read): `python -m pytest -q` → final log line: `61594 passed, 332 deselected in 102.16s (0:01:42)`.

Only `src/packaging/specifiers.py` was modified; no test files touched.
